text:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing a fleet-wide uptick in soft ECC and prober-linked resets in us-west2. Burst started ~08:05 UTC, capacity visible drop ~7.8%.
kevin: link to the dashboard?
maya: https://redwood.internal/metrics/us-west2/gpu-ecc?from=08:00&to=09:00 — top hosts clustered in rack-7 and rack-9.
prober-bot: ALERT: gpu-prober error rate > 5% (us-west2) — 2200 errors in last 15m — pager escalated.
liam: putting a quick probe: what does `rgpuctl list --errors` show?
maya: ran that on a subset, output snippet: ```
node-7a: soft-ecc: 124 (incr), xid-47: 18, last-reset: 08:03
node-7b: soft-ecc: 98 (incr), xid-47: 11, last-reset: 08:06
node-9c: soft-ecc: 140 (incr), xid-47: 25, last-reset: 08:07
```
sophia: customer load is now routing to regional fallback; latency SLOs for some users degraded by ~12%. We should throttle non-prod jobs.
kevin: can we triage whether this is HW (card) vs driver/prober bug? Any recent kernel/driver rollouts?
oncall-uk: FYI — we rolled a driver patch to nodes in rack-7 between 02:00–05:00 for NVDRV-2.1.4. Patch notes: "prober timeout handling improvement".
nora: that timing lines up. If prober timeouts increased, it could exaggerate soft-ecc counters. Recommend rolling back driver on a small canary to validate.
liam: I can stage a rollback on node-7b and 9c. Plan: drain, rollback-driver, uncordon, watch 15m. Anyone object?
sophia: please mark traffic-surge-override so we don't evict customer jobs unexpectedly.
maya: running drain on 7b now: `kubectl drain node-7b --ignore-daemonsets --force`.
maya: journal tail from node-7b: ```
Mar 17 08:02:59 node-7b kernel: NVRM: Xid (0001:00000047) at 0x... resetting GPU
Mar 17 08:03:01 node-7b gpu-prober[2345]: probe timeout for gpu0, restarting check
Mar 17 08:03:02 node-7b kernel: NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed!
```
kevin: that's the xid-47 pattern. HW could still be noisy, but prober restart + kernel RmInit suggests driver interaction. Good canary.
liam: rollback command staged: `sudo dpkg -i /opt/drivers/nvdrv-2.1.3.deb && systemctl restart gpu-prober`. Starting now on node-7b.
prober-bot: INFO: gpu-prober restarted on node-7b by liam.
maya: after rollback, soft-ecc went from 98 -> 3 over 6m on 7b. node-9c still noisy.
liam: that strongly implicates the 2.1.4 driver changes. I'll roll 2.1.3 on remaining rack-7 canaries (7a,7c) then pause.
sophia: please open a support ticket with the driver vendor with logs attached — we need root cause and if 2.1.4 has a regression.
kevin: creating ticket TCK-4281. Attaching `dmesg`, `gpu-prober` logs, and `rgpuctl` dumps from 7a/7b/9c.
nora: ops note — we should consider a short-term policy to avoid auto-upgrading drivers across multiple racks simultaneously. Add to runbook.
maya: agreed. I'm updating the emergency runbook (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-ecc-triage) with rollback steps + canary checklist.
ops-bot: SCHEDULED: rolling drain/rollback plan initiated for racks [7, ?]. ETA for complete canary test 35m. Notifying eng-infra for capacity plan.
liam: coordinating with eng-infra: can we provision 6 spare GPUs in us-east to soften customer impact?
oncall-uk: Eng-infra acknowledged, provisioning 6 spare GPUs (temp burst) — will ping when available.
maya: summary: driver 2.1.4 appears correlated with soft-ecc + xid-47 wave in us-west2; rollback to 2.1.3 on canaries reduced errors. Next steps: hold 2.1.4 rollout, widen rollbacks if canaries stable, vendor ticket TCK-4281, temporary capacity burst, runbook update.
sophia: thanks — please post a short update for support and #status page once we have vendor confirmation.
maya: will do. tagging @oncall-uk for follow-ups and @kevin for vendor comms. :thumbsup:
kevin: ack, will draft vendor packet and attach the logs.
maya: I'll keep this thread updated with roll status and final remediation notes.
